key_impacts: Children and adolescents were hit the hardest by the disaster in Uttarakhand.
A 16-year-old stable-hand (Anil) died in Kedarnath when the Mandakini river, fuelled by incessant rains, swept across the town on 17 June 2013.
A mule/horse operator in Kedarnath went missing, removing the sole breadwinner from Pinky’s family and threatening her ability to continue schooling.
The disaster caused widespread loss of life and property and disrupted basic services across Uttarakhand for months.

key_impacts: The State Primary School at Farkia was transformed into a pile of rubble by the landslide.
For two weeks after the catastrophe, the school operated from two makeshift locations in the village.
From 13 August, classes shifted to the Panchayat premises, where damp conditions impeded teaching and learning.
Seven months after the building’s destruction, there was still no indication of reconstruction.
